stem.text: What is the mechanism for the reaction of ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, with hydrogen cyanide, $\text{HCN}$, in the presence of $\text{NaCN}$?

A.alt: Curly-arrow mechanism: CH3CHO plus :CN- adds to the carbonyl carbon giving CH3CH(O-)CN; the H is then removed as H- to give CH3COCN plus H-

B.alt: Curly-arrow mechanism: CH3CHO plus :CN- gives CH3CH(O-)CN; this takes up H from H-CN, giving CH3CH(OH)CN plus :CN-

C.alt: Curly-arrow mechanism: the carbonyl O of CH3CHO takes H from HCN, giving the carbocation CH3CH(+)OH; :CN- then attacks it to give CH3CH(OH)CN

D.alt: Radical mechanism: initiation HCN to H• and •CN; propagation CH3CHO + •CN to CH3CH(O•)CN, then with HCN to CH3CH(OH)CN and •CN; termination CH3CH(O•)CN + H• to CH3CH(OH)CN
